news.title: US storms leave more than 260,000 without power as Thanksgiving travel disruption continues
news.text:
More than 260,000 people remain without electricity after severe storms affected both coasts of the United States over the Thanksgiving holiday.

A powerful system brought strong winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding to the eastern US on Thursday. Pennsylvania was the state worst affected by power cuts early on Friday, according to monitoring website Poweroutage.us.

Conditions have begun to improve, although forecasters warned recovery would take time. The West Coast was also hit by separate storms.

The weather continued to cause disruption for travellers on Friday, one of the busiest days of the holiday period. More than 3,400 flights within, into or out of the US were delayed, while nearly 670 were cancelled.

On Thanksgiving Day, more than 2,500 flights were delayed and more than 450 cancelled, according to Flightaware.com. One passenger told the BBC he had spent 13 hours stranded at New York’s LaGuardia Airport while attempting to travel to Chicago to visit friends.

The effects of the storms were widespread along the East Coast. US President Donald Trump said he would consider releasing emergency funds to assist those affected.

Severe winds forced bridges to close in Maryland, while large waves hit beaches in Delaware and water spread onto the boardwalk. Washington experienced its wettest Thanksgiving on record, with tidal water surging onto the runways at Reagan Washington National Airport.

Parts of several states, including New York, declared states of emergency overnight between Thursday and Friday.

Almost 2in (5cm) of rain fell in New York City’s Central Park, according to preliminary data from the National Weather Service (NWS). That made it the wettest Thanksgiving recorded at the site.

The annual Macy’s Thanksgiving parade in New York was also postponed until Saturday. It was the first postponement in the event’s 100-year history.

Neighbouring New Jersey reported several road and bridge closures, while photographs and videos showed floodwater covering streets in cities across the state. Coastal flood warnings remained in place for parts of New Jersey through Friday evening.

In a video posted on social media, a blogger based in Ocean City, New Jersey, described the situation as “wild” while wading through water that reached above his waist.

news.title: Trump and Nvidia: Good for stocks, worrying for investors?
news.text:
“Probably.” That was Donald Trump’s response when asked whether the recent market sell-off had influenced his intervention to secure the return of Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s chief executive.

Trump’s response captures the so-called Trump put, the belief he will step in to support stocks when they fall far enough.

This is the third such example, notes Interactive Brokers’ Steve Sosnick, during the second Trump administration. The first was in April 2025, when Trump reversed course after stocks tanked following his Liberation Day tariffs. Next came March 2026, when Trump’s hopeful messages about peace talks with Iran prompted a sharp recovery in stocks. 

Trump will have been pleased by the market’s response this time too, with Nvidia surging 31 per cent in a day and the S&P 500 rebounding sharply, even if volatility remains elevated.

Bloomberg analyst Eric Balchunas identifies three such props underpinning the market: the Trump put, the Fed put (Federal Reserve support when markets fall hard), and what he calls the Vanguard put (the relentless flow of money into index funds and retirement plans, with millions of investors buying in good times and bad).

These forces are why Balchunas prefers to remain a long-term bull, saying he’d “rather create wealth than sound smart”.

There is much to be said for this. However, while the Trump put comes with obvious benefits, it comes with a cost. There is a big difference between a president reversing a damaging tariff policy to calm markets, and intervening so decisively (“I made the deal”) in the internal affairs of a publicly listed company.

The latter, cautions Kyle Chan of the Brookings Institution, “sounds much more like Beijing than Washington”.

Nell Minow of ValueEdge Advisors is also concerned, writing in the Financial Times that Trump’s involvement “is a strong signal to other big companies about what is allowed or even encouraged”.

It’s all very well having a stocks-obsessed president, but the danger is that Trump erodes the very institutional foundations that have long made US markets so attractive to investors.
news.summary: The US president’s intervention ‘sounds much more like Beijing than Washington’
news.author: Proinsias O'Mahony

news.title: Nvidia Blackwell Tech Used At China Site Tied To 'Spy' Alice Huang
news.text: A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp.'s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, the woman at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker. The gear installed at the Yangtze River Delta Project included a GB300 NVL72 rack, among Nvidia's most powerful products, according to a serial number specified in documents submitted to Chinese regulators in November. Shanghai Shuoyao offered the hardware as collateral to obtain a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, according to filings from the lender that were reviewed by Bloomberg News.A second firm, Shanghai Kezhan, controlled by a Tokyo-based parent, described a GB200 server - which also relies on Blackwell chips - at the facility. That description was provided in documents when it obtained a 90 million yuan loan in late 2025 from a finance-leasing firm wholly owned by a local Shanghai government agency.After initially dipping as much as 2.6% in New York trading on Friday, the shares gained less than 1% to $150.49. The submissions reveal for the first time that Nvidia's Blackwell processors found their way into a Chinese data center that has ties to Alice Huang and Megaspeed. These processors were until recently Nvidia's most powerful data center products, and they've always been illegal to ship to China without a US license. President Donald Trump has explicitly said he doesn't want these chips - which OpenAI and Anthropic PBC use to train their most cutting-edge models - going to the Asian country, at least for now. Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, meanwhile, once claimed they were too big to smuggle: a standard two-meter-tall GB300 NVL72 server rack, which contains 72 Blackwell Ultra chips and 36 Grace processors, can weigh more than 1,500 kilograms (3,300 pounds) and is about the size of a gigantic fridge.Nvidia and its just-reinstated CEO have come under intense scrutiny in recent weeks for their failure to stop diversion of the company's products to China, a shadow trade that US officials believe is worth billions of dollars. It's unclear how the GB300 rack made its way to the country, to Shanghai Shuoyao or to this specific site - described in local media as designed to house as many as 800,000 servers. By inputting the serial number for the product into a public warranty database, Bloomberg found that it was manufactured by Taiwan's Gigabyte Technology Co., which assembles Nvidia chips into servers and racks. The database also provided a model name for the serial number, which matches a GB300 NVL72 server rack manufactured by the Taiwanese company. This sort of gear often passes through several hands - including local distribution networks - before it's installed in data centers. In many cases, products that were ultimately smuggled into China were originally sold to parties in unrestricted areas. Bloomberg provided the rack's serial number to Gigabyte, seeking information about to whom Gigabyte had originally sold the hardware and when. It declined to answer those questions, citing company policy. The firm "conducts all business in compliance with applicable laws and regulations," a spokesperson said in an emailed statement. "All transactions are subject to our internal compliance requirements and the relevant laws and regulations in effect at the time."Shanghai Shuoyao - the company that procured the GB300 rack and offered it as collateral - is active at the data center linked to Alice Huang and also has significant overlap with Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is under US investigation over concerns that it smuggled Nvidia chips to China, Bloomberg has reported. Shanghai Shuoyao, which hasn't responded to Bloomberg queries over the past year, confirmed this month in a rare public statement that it is one of Megaspeed's service providers, describing the partnership as "limited to ordinary commercial cooperation." Megaspeed, meanwhile, used a rendering of the Yangtze River Delta Project in 2024 to describe its largest data center to investors, dubbing the site a "specific area" facility in an unnamed country. Bloomberg does not have evidence that Megaspeed itself diverted Nvidia hardware there, and Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing in response to the US probe. The company has not answered repeated queries about the Yangtze River Delta Project. Nor has Nvidia, which for years insisted that there was no black market for its products and didn't respond to questions for this story. The Trump administration this month put Megaspeed on a US trade blacklist, citing a significant risk of involvement in chip diversion.Alice Huang in 2023 founded Megaspeed, a so-called neocloud that won a coveted stamp of approval from Nvidia within four days of its creation, and went on to become the chipmaker's largest Southeast Asian customer. She also has ties to a number of companies that invested in the Yangtze River Delta Project, which counts Kang Wei as its president. Kang has been introduced at times as Alice Huang's romantic partner, people familiar with the matter said.It's unclear how far along operators are in meeting their overall goal for that project, which at 800,000 servers would be on par with hyperscale facilities used by companies like OpenAI. It's also unclear what mix of servers they plan to use. The parameters they've outlined in construction plans reviewed by Bloomberg - specifically, the total processing power as compared to the energy input - would be extremely difficult to satisfy with chips from Chinese companies such as Huawei Technologies Co. Still, the smuggled hardware disclosed in the filings reviewed by Bloomberg is just a fraction of what they'd need. These documents only cover hardware offered as collateral for loans - providing a small snapshot of the operators' ambitions, while also underscoring how some Chinese financial institutions, including with government ties, were aware that restricted hardware was getting into China and willing to lend capital on those assets. Bloomberg was unable to reach the leasing company that lent money to Shanghai Kezhan, nor Shanghai Innovation Bank, which in addition to the money it lent Shanghai Shuoyao, also provided a 200 million yuan loan to another company called Shanghai Longjie, similarly with restricted Nvidia chips as collateral. Shanghai Longjie - which has the same parent company as Shanghai Shuoyao - disclosed in documents filed to regulators that it has servers containing Nvidia's earlier Hopper-generation chips, which are illegal to ship to China without Washington's permission, Bloomberg reported this month. That hardware was manufactured by Super Micro Computer Inc. and Dell Technologies Inc. It's unclear whether the shipments had US approval.Those aren't the only Hopper chips at the Yangtze River Delta Project. Shanghai Kezhan, the company that described the GB200 server in filings last year, also disclosed that it has 32 servers with H200 chips there. These products had a Gigabyte prefix in their model name, but the documents didn't include serial numbers - making them harder to trace. Shanghai Kezhan is headquartered about half a kilometer from the Yangtze River Delta Project, at the same commercial complex where Shanghai Shuoyao solicited engineers to work on Nvidia H100 and H200 chips - two restricted models. In February 2024, both of these firms added "imports and exports" to their business activities, according to data from Qizhidao, a company information provider. The same month, Megaspeed's original parent - the Chinese gaming giant 7Road - obtained 16.7% of Shanghai Kezhan via a subsidiary the gaming company bought from Alice Huang in 2019. The other 83.3% of Kezhan is ultimately owned by NeXPower Japan, according to Qizhidao. Japan's official companies registry returned only one company named NeXPower, which was established in March 2025. Caixin, a Chinese business news outlet, said the Tokyo firm is controlled by Alice Huang.Bloomberg has been unable to reach NeXPower for comment. Chinese-speaking staffers at the firm's registered address wouldn't confirm that was NeXPower's office, and shut the door after Bloomberg News asked about their relationship with Alice Huang and Shanghai Kezhan. On the intercom was a message saying they are working and will not respond to media questions. The registered address of the company's director appeared to be a vacated residence.In May 2025, records compiled by Big Trade Data show, Shanghai Kezhan received a shipment worth $11 million, flown from Malaysia to Shanghai Pudong International Airport with the company as consignee.The customs document described the shipment as "storage chassis," referring to a structure that houses components of a storage server. But the product code it was assigned to was 847150, which denotes computing servers. The shipment's unit price was $264,108, too costly for a storage chassis - but within the price range of servers powered by Nvidia's Hopper chips.(Except for the headline, this story has not been edited by NDTV staff and is published from a syndicated feed.)

news.title: Despite Midterm Sweep, Trump Can Fulfill His Day One Promise to Americans
news.text:
A newly empowered progressive-led Democrat coalition is preparing to settle into its majority on Capitol Hill and has made no secret of its determination to complicate President Trump’s final two years.

The incoming majority, however, does not get a veto over everything his administration can do. The president still retains considerable executive authority to deliver on the America First agenda that has been his rallying cry for the last decade.

Even before stepping onto the political scene, Donald Trump urged more balanced trade relations built on reciprocity and fairness. In fact, it is arguably the singular defining feature of his lifelong worldview. In a 1987 interview with Larry King, Trump remarked that “people are tired of watching the other countries ripping off the United States.” And nearly three decades later, at the infancy of his formal political career, his stump speeches frequently focused on China taking advantage of U.S. trade policy, often referring to our country as the “piggy bank that’s being robbed.” He echoed that language throughout his first term and returned to it as recently as July, when he lashed out at the European Union for treating America as a piggy bank and called for a Section 301 trade investigation into “the practice of robbing American companies and, in turn, the American taxpayer.”

Now, even more than before, formally initiating this investigation into Europe’s predatory digital trade practices is an opportunity to reinforce President Trump’s commitment to standing up for American interests. With a large portion of his agenda now likely to be stonewalled by congressional Democrats, prioritizing wins that don’t require congressional approval just makes sense.

Europe has certainly earned the scrutiny.

Our so-called allies across the pond have spent years invoking “digital sovereignty” and “consumer protection” to justify taxing, restricting, investigating, and fining America’s technology companies billions of dollars for the crime of outperforming their European competitors.

France’s Europe Minister Benjamin Haddad recently touted the roughly $5 billion Europe stood to collect from a single Google antitrust fine as “a new revenue stream” that can be used to lower member states’ contributions to the EU budget. Haddad is saying the quiet part out loud — and it’s exactly what President Trump has warned about for decades.

EU lawmakers are now considering a way for their telecom companies to collect, too. Just this month, the European Parliament’s industry committee took up draft changes to the already controversial proposed Digital Networks Act that could let those carriers charge American technology companies “network usage fees” — effectively making them subsidize Europe’s telecom industry — despite the EU’s commitment in its 2025 trade agreement with the United States not to implement such fees.

Beyond helping themselves to American companies’ money, European officials have been equally aggressive in asserting control over how those companies operate, using regulations like the Digital Markets Act and Digital Services Act to force changes to their products and, in some cases, to pressure platforms to censor political speech. All the while, the bloc is putting up billions of euros in public funding for AI infrastructure and sovereign-cloud contracts and advancing its newly unveiled “Tech Sovereignty Package” to prop up European competitors and reduce reliance on foreign (primarily American) providers.

The pretense is embarrassingly transparent. European leaders are using government power to stop American companies from succeeding where their own firms have failed to compete. They are propping up inferior European alternatives to the very American companies that have provided Europe’s digital infrastructure and now seek to make American companies — and ultimately American taxpayers — subsidize European carriers as well.

A formal examination of these discriminatory practices is very much in order. Through Section 301, USTR can establish grounds for penalties that would give European officials ample reason to change course. Absent increased pressure, what is their incentive to do so?

The investigation could also strengthen the case for applying pressure through other avenues, including federal contracting.

European companies continue to receive billions of dollars in American taxpayer-funded business even as their governments deny our companies fair treatment abroad. If the 301 investigation confirms what the evidence already suggests, those firms should have no reason to assume that business will remain unaffected.

For example, the Department of War could reconsider whether awarding future contracts to companies such as European SAP, Siemens, Publicis Groupe, and Accenture serves American interests. The Federal Communications Commission could reconsider the approvals that allow Deutsche Telekom to hold a majority stake in T-Mobile. The German carrier’s unrelenting support for the very regulations and network fees that threaten American companies’ ability to operate in Europe could carry particular weight as the agency reassesses the terms on which the carrier operates here.

American companies have earned their success by developing technology that powers businesses, industries, and economies around the world — and Europe has grown far too comfortable penalizing them. Even with a less-than-cooperative Congress following the 2026 midterms, the Trump administration still has the authority, and obligation, to follow through on his commitment to defend American companies against blatantly unfair treatment abroad. It’s time to open President Trump’s investigation.

John Czwartacki is the founder and President of Public Policy Solutions. He served in senior roles at OMB and CFPB during the first Trump administration.

news.title: Report: Half a Dozen Trump Officials Moved into Military Housing amid Iranian Death Threats
news.text:
Roughly half a dozen Trump administration officials are now living in military housing in the Washington, DC, area as mounting threats against senior U.S. officials, including Iranian assassination plots, have prompted extraordinary security measures.

CNN reported Friday that a historically high number of civilian administration officials are residing on military installations, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, War Secretary Pete Hegseth, White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, and Attorney General Todd Blanche.

Bessent, who has spearheaded the Trump administration’s campaign to economically cripple the Iranian regime, is the latest known Cabinet official to relocate to military housing.

As Breitbart News previously reported, the threats against the Treasury secretary had reached what a senior administration official described as “more than an advanced stage.”

Bessent has since publicly addressed the threats, making clear that his relocation came at the direction of the Secret Service and that Tehran’s efforts to intimidate him would not deter the administration from intensifying its economic pressure campaign.

“F the Iranian leadership,” Bessent declared this month, characterizing the threats against his life as evidence that the administration’s Operation Economic Outcast was working.

The Treasury secretary also accused the Wall Street Journal of “reckless journalism” over its publication of photographs of his private residence despite requests that the newspaper refrain from doing so.

The threats against Bessent come amid broader intelligence warnings about Tehran’s efforts to target Americans both at home and abroad.

Earlier this month, U.S. intelligence reportedly indicated that Iran was exploring the use of a radiological “dirty bomb” or chemical weapons to target senior American officials in Washington, though the White House maintained that there were no credible threats to the homeland.

The revelations followed the disclosure of an unclassified intelligence memorandum in late October in which Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Rubio that Iranian assassination plots against Americans abroad had reached “advanced stages.”

Clayton subsequently warned Congress that Iranian threats against Americans had “substantially increased.”

“Our women and men abroad, our women and men here in the United States, are under greater threat,” he told the House Homeland Security Committee.

While Rubio has stressed that U.S. intelligence has not identified an imminent threat of a dirty-bomb attack in Washington, President Donald Trump has warned that Iran would face devastating consequences if it attacked the United States.

“They will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before,” Trump said.

The heightened security concerns also come as Asif Merchant, a Pakistani national trained by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), was sentenced last week to 27 and a half years in prison for his role in a thwarted Iranian-directed assassination conspiracy targeting Trump and other American political figures.

Iranian threats, however, are not the only security concerns prompting senior administration officials to relocate.

Blanche also recently moved into military housing over security concerns, CNN reported, citing people familiar with the matter. His predecessor, Pam Bondi, had similarly relocated to a military installation last year.

Miller and his family relocated last year after their private residence became the target of a harassment campaign, amid heightened concerns over political violence following the assassination of Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk.

“The Millers relocated because there was an elaborate, well-documented stalking, doxing, and threat campaign targeting their residence,” the White House told the outlet.

The relocations come amid a broader surge in threats against public officials, with U.S. Secret Service Director Sean Curran recently describing the threat environment as the most challenging he has witnessed in his 24-year career.

Senior Secret Service officials told reporters that the agency had handled 10,000 threat-related cases involving its protectees this year, with threats increasing by 40 percent over the previous year.

“The threat picture and environment is as large as I’ve ever seen it,” Curran said.

While the practice of housing civilian Cabinet officials on military installations predates the current Trump administration, the number currently doing so represents a significant departure from previous administrations.

Robert Gates became the first defense secretary to reside in military housing under President George W. Bush. In 2008, the Pentagon argued that housing Gates on a military installation would save taxpayers the cost of establishing and maintaining round-the-clock security at a private residence.

Congress subsequently established a rental arrangement requiring defense secretaries to pay five percent more than a four-star general or admiral.

Rep. George Whitesides (D-CA), meanwhile, secured House Armed Services Committee approval for a Pentagon report, due next spring, examining the security threats behind the relocations, the legal authority for housing political appointees on military installations, and whether the officials are paying fair market rental rates.

A White House official told CNN that while many Cabinet officials are unable to live in the city “due to targeted security threats,” they have personally contributed to the administration’s efforts to make the nation’s capital “safe and beautiful.”

Bessent, meanwhile, has vowed that Tehran’s threats will not deter the administration from pursuing its economic pressure campaign.

“I’m not going to be cowered,” he said. “They have initiated death threats against me and other members of the Cabinet. We’re not going to be cowered.”

Joshua Klein is a reporter for Breitbart News. Email him at jklein@breitbart.com. Follow him on Twitter @JoshuaKlein.

Roughly half a dozen Trump administration officials are now living in military housing in the Washington, DC, area as mounting threats against senior U.S. officials, including Iranian assassination plots, have prompted extraordinary security measures.

news.title: Biden’s ‘startlingly dull’ memoir flops
news.text:
Former US President Joe Biden’s memoir sold just 21,000 copies in its first week despite the author reportedly receiving a $10 million advance, multiple media outlets reported on Friday, citing market research firm Circana.

Critics described the 480-page book, Promise Me, America, released on November 17, as offering few new insights and faulted the 84-year-old Democrat for failing to meaningfully reflect on his mistakes during his presidency from 2021 to 2025.

“Honestly, it’s like who the f**k cares anymore about Joe Biden,” a former Biden aide told the New York Post when asked about the poor sales.

According to AP, Barack Obama’s A Promised Land sold more than 1 million copies in its first week in 2020, while Bill Clinton’s My Life sold more than 1 million copies within two weeks in 2004.

Biden has done little to promote the book. The former president was diagnosed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer in May 2025.

Amy Davidson Sorkin of The New Yorker described Biden’s book as “startlingly dull,” writing that “much of it has the feel of something written by a committee – and a committee of which Biden himself need not have been a member.”

Writing for The New York Times, Jennifer Szalai argued that Biden was “awkward and defensive” when addressing two controversial aspects of his presidency: his handling of Israel’s war in Gaza and his decision to run for a second term.

Having served as Obama’s vice president for eight years, Biden was elected president in 2020. Despite initially portraying himself as a transitional leader and mounting concerns about his age and health, he sought reelection before abruptly withdrawing from the race less than four months before the vote. He endorsed Vice President Kamala Harris, who went on to lose to Donald Trump.
news.summary:
Joe Biden’s memoir sold just 21,000 copies in its first week, with critics panning the book as dull and defensive

news.title: Seoul monitoring signs of possible Kim Jong Un visit to China
news.text:
A fresh visit to Beijing by North Korean leader Kim Jong Un could pave the way for talks with Xi Jinping on recent US-China discussions and a possible trilateral summit involving Russia. (EPA Images pic)
SEOUL: South Korea's spy agency said Saturday it was monitoring "various developments" about a possible visit to China by North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, following reports on such a trip.
China is North Korea's largest trading partner and a vital source of diplomatic, economic and political support for Pyongyang, although ties have not always been smooth.
Kim made an unannounced, one-day visit to the Chinese border city of Dandong in October, crossing a major bridge linking China and nuclear-armed North Korea that is widely considered a symbol of their deepening economic ties.
A South Korean broadcaster KBS, citing an unnamed diplomatic source, reported that Chinese President Xi Jinping told his South Korean counterpart Lee Jae Myung during their summit earlier this month that Kim could visit China.
Citing an unnamed government source, it also reported that an "emergency order" had been issued in the Chinese border city of Dandong, echoing arrangements made for Kim's October visit.
Seoul's spy agency told AFP Saturday it was "keeping a close eye on various developments", when asked about the report.
Seoul's presidential office said Xi did not mention what was described by the KBS report, adding that the administration "is closely monitoring developments in North Korea-China relations".
Despite long-running UN sanctions, North Korea has enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state in law, with its regime repeatedly declaring its atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible.
Kim has ignored repeated overtures for talks from US President Donald Trump, who has said a meeting was "up to" China's Xi.
Experts say Pyongyang is effectively demanding US recognition as a nuclear-armed state as a precondition for talks - a concession they say would pose complex diplomatic and security challenges for Washington, a key ally of Seoul.
A visit to China could give Kim an opportunity to discuss with Xi the outcome of the recent US-China talks and trilateral summit involving Russia, another key ally of Pyongyang, experts say.
news.summary: South Korean broadcaster KBS, citing a diplomatic source, reported that Chinese president Xi Jinping told his South Korean counterpart Lee Jae Myung at their recent summit that Kim Jong Un could visit China.
news.author: AFP

news.title: From Ceasefire U-Turn to ‘Dictator’ Zelensky: 8 Times Trump Repeated Kremlin Narratives
news.text:
US presidential envoy Jared Kushner’s interview with Politico this week shed light on why Donald Trump’s once-insistent demand for an immediate ceasefire in Ukraine faded from Washington’s diplomatic agenda: Putin did not want one.

But the ceasefire reversal is far from the only instance in which Trump’s rhetoric has aligned with Moscow’s.

Here are eight examples of that convergence.

Abandoning the demand for a ceasefire before a peace deal

Before his August 2025 summit with Putin in Alaska, Trump had called for an immediate truce and threatened Russia with consequences if diplomatic efforts failed.

Following the summit, however, he argued that a comprehensive peace agreement could be negotiated while fighting continued.

Trump also adopted a rationale long advanced by Moscow – that a pause in hostilities would allow military forces to regroup and rearm.

“You have a cease-fire, and they rebuild and rebuild and rebuild,” Trump said during his Oval Office meeting with Zelensky.

Although Trump acknowledged that halting the fighting could save lives, he no longer considered it a prerequisite for a peace agreement.

More than a year after Anchorage, Moscow’s opposition to an immediate truce remains unchanged, as Kushner’s latest remarks made clear.

Portraying Putin as committed to peace

Despite Russia’s continued bombardment of Ukrainian cities, Trump has repeatedly insisted that Putin wants peace.

At the recent trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China, Trump again referred to Putin as his friend – a characterization that drew sharp criticism from Zelensky.

In an interview with the BBC published Thursday, Nov. 26, the Ukrainian president called Trump’s description of Putin “strange.”

“He’s an aggressor, and a killer,” Zelensky said, comparing such a friendship to declaring friendship with Adolf Hitler during World War II.

Trump’s envoy Jared Kushner, meanwhile, praised Putin’s political skills this week, describing the Russian leader as a “grandmaster of politics.”

Calling Zelensky a ‘dictator’ and questioning his legitimacy

The Kremlin has repeatedly sought to challenge Zelensky’s legitimacy since the expiration of his initial five-year presidential term in May 2024.

On Feb. 19, 2025, Trump echoed that characterization, calling the Ukrainian president a “dictator without elections.”

Zelensky was democratically elected in 2019, winning more than 73% of the vote in the presidential runoff.

Ukrainian law prohibits presidential elections under martial law, while the country’s constitution provides for the incumbent president to remain in office until a successor assumes the presidency.

The restrictions are a consequence of martial law imposed following Russia’s full-scale invasion, rather than a unilateral decision by Zelensky to cancel elections.

Moscow has used the absence of wartime elections to question Zelensky’s authority to negotiate and sign a potential peace agreement.

Suggesting Ukraine must accept territorial losses

Moscow has repeatedly insisted that any peace settlement must recognize what it calls the “new territorial realities” created by its occupation of Ukrainian land.

Trump has similarly questioned Ukraine’s ability to restore its internationally recognized borders.

In an interview with CBS’s 60 Minutes on Nov. 8, 2026, Trump suggested that Ukraine would emerge from the war with altered territorial boundaries.

“They’re going to end up with a little bit different shape,” Trump said.

Kyiv has consistently rejected legal recognition of Russia’s occupation, maintaining that its sovereignty and territorial integrity cannot be compromised through military coercion.

Characterizing Russia’s invasion as a ‘proxy war’

Putin has long portrayed Russia’s invasion of Ukraine as part of a broader confrontation with the West, arguing that Western governments are using Ukraine to weaken Russia.

Senior Trump administration officials have adopted similar terminology.

Speaking on the MD Meets podcast on Wednesday, Nov. 25, Kushner characterized Russia’s invasion as a proxy conflict.

“It’s effectively become a proxy war where Europe is funding and arming Ukraine against Russia,” Kushner said.

European governments maintain that their military assistance enables Ukraine to exercise its internationally recognized right to self-defense under the UN Charter.

Opposing Ukraine’s NATO membership

Preventing Ukraine from joining NATO has long been one of Putin’s principal foreign policy objectives.

In December 2021, two months before launching the full-scale invasion, Moscow demanded guarantees against further NATO enlargement, alongside restrictions on the alliance’s military presence in Eastern Europe.

Trump has repeatedly expressed sympathy for Russia’s objections to Ukraine joining the alliance.

Speaking at the White House on Feb. 13, 2025, Trump said he could not see how Russia would accept Ukraine’s NATO membership.

His remarks followed the Kremlin’s public endorsement of his earlier statements blaming the Biden administration for raising the prospect of Ukrainian membership.

Washington has presented its position as a pragmatic assessment of what could be achieved through negotiations.

Kyiv maintains that its sovereign right to determine its security arrangements cannot be subject to a Russian veto.

Shifting responsibility for Russia’s war onto Ukraine

Since launching its full-scale invasion, Moscow has repeatedly sought to shift responsibility for the conflict onto Ukraine and its Western partners.

Trump echoed that framing in February 2025 when he suggested Ukraine could have avoided the war by reaching an agreement with Russia.

“You should have never started it,” Trump said on Feb. 18, addressing Ukraine’s leadership.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion on Feb. 24, 2022, eight years after illegally annexing Crimea and beginning its military intervention in eastern Ukraine.

The issue resurfaced this week following Trump’s Nov. 25 meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte at Mar-a-Lago.

Their joint statement specifically called on Russia to avoid actions that could expand the war.

However, when Trump subsequently published the statement on Truth Social, he added Ukraine to the warning, changing the wording agreed upon with the NATO chief.

Describing Russian attacks on Ukrainian civilians as mistakes

Russian officials have routinely denied deliberately targeting Ukrainian civilians, often claiming that Russian forces strike military objectives.

Following Russia’s deadly Palm Sunday attack on the northeastern Ukrainian city of Sumy on April 13, 2025, Trump suggested that the strike had been a mistake.

“They made a mistake,” Trump said, without presenting evidence supporting that assessment.

Although Trump described the attack as terrible, his administration subsequently declined to support a joint G7 statement condemning the Russian strike.

Trump has repeatedly defended his approach to Putin as a negotiating strategy, arguing that maintaining communication with the Russian leader is essential to ending the war.
news.summary: US presidential envoy Jared Kushner’s latest interview shed light on why Donald Trump abandoned his demand for an immediate ceasefire in Ukraine. But the reversal is far from an isolated example. From questioning Zelensky’s legitimacy and opposing Ukraine’s NATO membership to suggesting territorial concessions and shifting responsibility for the war, Trump and members of his administration have repeatedly echoed Kremlin narratives.

news.title: Trump to keep suspense over his successor for as long as possible — NYP
news.text:
NEW YORK, November 28. /TASS/. US President Donald Trump intends to delay revealing which Republican contender he plans to endorse in the 2028 presidential race for as long as possible, New York Post reported, citing a source.

As noted, he "savors fomenting competition among his team." He will likely refrain from officially endorsing any of the Republican contenders for the 2028 U.S. presidential race until the very last moment. By doing so, Trump expects to retain control over the Republicans and avoid becoming a "lame duck" prematurely - a term used for politicians whose influence diminishes as their term nears its end or as they lose control over the political system.

In an interview with New York Post, Trump said there is a "certain group of people" among Republicans who could run for president. The newspaper recalled that over the past year, Trump has not ruled out that either Vice President JD Vance or Secretary of State Marco Rubio could become his successor. During the interview, the US leader was asked whether Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth could run for president. "He’s doing a good job," Trump replied.

Earlier, US media outlets, citing sources, reported that Hegseth was considering running for president in 2028. The defense secretary subsequently denied those reports.

news.title: Trump official calls Markwayne Mullin an 'idiot and liberal' amid claims DHS boss wishes he'd never taken the job
news.text:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has reportedly been privately telling people he wishes he had never left the Senate to join Donald Trump's cabinet – and some inside the White House apparently share his regret.

The former Oklahoma senator, who took charge of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) in March, is facing growing discontent within the administration following a turbulent series of national security incidents, technology failures and controversial trips.

His political fortunes have reportedly sunk so low that some White House staffers have even started taking bets on how much longer he will remain in the job.

Mullin, 49, has allegedly confided in others that he would rather have remained on Capitol Hill, according to a report by the New York Post.

'He's telling people he wished he stayed in the Senate,' a source with connections to DHS told the newspaper, claiming to have heard the admission directly from Mullin.

Two additional sources said they had been made aware of similar remarks by the secretary.

But one White House official delivered a particularly brutal assessment of the former plumbing company owner.

'I wish he had stayed at his plumbing company,' the official told the Post. 'He's an idiot. Terrible messenger and liberal.'

Mullin furiously rejected the report, insisting he had no regrets about joining the administration.

'This is complete and total fake news. I love the DHS mission. They should be ashamed of this FALSE story,' he said.

Among the most politically damaging claims is that Mullin has fallen out of favor with Trump's powerful new White House chief of staff, Stephen Miller.

Miller is reportedly dissatisfied with Mullin's management of several recent crises and personally intervened to reduce his involvement in the administration's response to a succession of technological disruptions.

The secretary came under intense scrutiny earlier this month when a nationwide ground stop brought American aviation to a standstill on November 13.

During a White House briefing alongside Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, Mullin attributed the chaos to modernization work that had overwhelmed aging air traffic control infrastructure.

But with thousands of passengers still dealing with the fallout from the disruption the following day, Mullin boarded a government aircraft bound for Baton Rouge, Louisiana, to attend a college football game between Texas and LSU.

The decision triggered widespread criticism.

Mullin subsequently embarked on an overseas trip with his wife, Christie, visiting Jordan, Azerbaijan, and the United Arab Emirates.

During his absence, JPMorgan Chase disclosed a cybersecurity breach that potentially exposed customers' personal information, while the CIA and two other American intelligence agencies also reported being hacked.

Further questions about Mullin's standing emerged this week when Miller publicly thanked administration officials involved in the successful destruction of a stockpile of lead explosives in Iowa.

Although the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), which operates under Mullin's department, was heavily involved, Miller singled out FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton without mentioning the Homeland Security secretary.

The two men have also reportedly differed over the implementation of Trump's aggressive immigration enforcement policies.

Miller, a driving force behind the president's mass deportation efforts, is said to favor a tougher approach than Mullin.

Trump himself intervened over the summer to overturn restrictions Mullin had imposed on vehicle pursuits.

The Washington Post has separately reported that White House staffers organized a betting pool on Mullin's longevity in the administration, although several officials questioned the extent of the sweepstakes.

'I saw that story and got upset I wasn't invited,' one aide joked to the New York Post.

Despite leaving Congress eight months ago, Mullin still regularly returns to Capitol Hill for early morning exercise sessions with his former colleagues.

'Markwayne Mullin still works out with us,' Georgia Republican Congressman Buddy Carter revealed. 'In fact, he leads the workout group.'

The former mixed martial arts fighter entered Congress in 2013 and served in the House before spending three years in the Senate.

A DHS spokesperson categorically denied suggestions that Mullin was unhappy in his new position.

'These anonymous, unsubstantiated claims are absurd and completely FALSE. Secretary Mullin has consistently said that the DHS mission is the greatest job he's ever had, thanks to the leadership of President Trump,' the spokesperson said.

'When President Trump asked him to serve in his cabinet, Secretary Mullin accepted the challenge and never looked back. He considers it the greatest honor of his life.'

The department also dismissed allegations of tensions with Miller, accusing those behind the claims of attempting to 'sow division and create an illusion of chaos.'

The White House maintained that the pair 'have forged a close bond' through their work tackling fraud, narcotics trafficking, terrorism and overseas scam operations.

Trump publicly defended Mullin during an Oval Office interview on Tuesday.

'He's a good person. He works very hard - I think he's been working very hard,' the president said.

But in an awkward exchange, Trump appeared unaware that his Homeland Security secretary was overseas.

'He's in the Middle East?' Trump asked, turning to White House communications director Steven Cheung.

'He's on a planned trip to meet his counterparts in some of the countries,' Cheung explained.

One factor that could ultimately help Mullin retain his position is the Republicans' midterm election defeat.

With Democrats set to assume control of the Senate on January 3, securing confirmation for a replacement Homeland Security secretary could become considerably more difficult for Trump.

The Daily Mail has contacted DHS and the White House for comment.
news.summary: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin reportedly regrets leaving the Senate to join Trump's cabinet, with some White House insiders sharing that sentiment.

news.title: When peace given no chance
news.text:
As a possibly unique case of a British immigrant to Argentina in the year 1982 who ended up working 34 years for the Buenos Aires Herald, how could this columnist not make seeing the powerful Malvinas war play Campo Minado (Minefield, in English) the centre of his week? As a play about memory and tackling the most difficult issues, it was picked by the Herald as a fitting way of marking its 150th anniversary this year and staged at the downtown Teatro Coliseo with a little help from some friends (last two performances this weekend) – Daniel Grinbank’s DG Experience and the British Council. And it just so happens that this review will be published on the 36th anniversary of Margaret Thatcher’s last day as prime minister.

Arriving in Argentina four months after the end of the war, this columnist could not claim to be an eye-witness, living and working in Hamburg during those 74 days. Since the German media had only a passing interest in the conflict, the only way to follow it closely was to listen continually to BFBS (British Forces Broadcasting Service, the radio for the British troops still occupying northwestern Germany at that time) – hardly the most impartial source. But at least the war forms part of my living memory – looking around the full house at the Teatro Coliseo, this reviewer concluded that not much more than 10 percent of the audience at best could say the same. Hence the vital importance of this play.

To say that Campo Minado is a call for peace is both to convey its central message and to fall short. The question it poses is not so much who can argue with peace as who should argue for it? Donald Trump launches his Board of Peace but gives the impression of being bored with peace much of the time. Beauty contestants almost invariably place world peace at the top of their wish lists but somehow this lacks the force of this play’s genuine veterans who have learned the value of peace through the bitterest experiences.

Just as you cannot have day without night or light without shadow, so peace is merely an abstraction without entering fully into the horrors of war. Nor is there any denialism about having been warriors 44 years ago on the part of these veterans now crusading for peace. Just before the grand finale – when Tip Cullen (standing in for Lou Armour) belts out such challenges to the audience over the rock music as “Have you ever seen a dead body?” or “Have you ever held a dead man in your arms?” – the two sides man their trenches and argue their cases in the sovereignty dispute, starting with the Malvinas being discovered by John Davis in 1592 versus being a stepping-stone in Magellan’s 1519-1922 circumnavigation of the world through to United Nations resolutions versus the 2013 referendum on the islands. Three men speak English throughout and three Spanish.

Time to meet the cast. Lou Armour was a key figure in launching this play 10 years ago as a rare case of being directly part of the war from start to finish – one of the 68 Royal Marines surrendering to Argentine forces in Stanley on April 2 and there for the Argentine surrender on June 14. With his replacement by Tip Cullen (an actor since ending his military service) the play loses authenticity but gains dramatic force.

David Jackson is the only British member of the original cast in these performances and the only one never on the front line despite coming from a family with several generations of military service – he spent the war decoding radio messages and is now a psychologist, giving free therapy in the play to Marcelo Vallejo.

Gurkha Sukrim Rai could not come due to a domestic accident but is not absent in the play. He serves to show that truth is the first casualty of war (while also exposing a certain latent racism in Argentina) – amongst other misreporting (such as sinking HMS Invincible, which only went to the scrapyard in 2011), Argentine propaganda media stated that over 300 prisoners-of-war had been massacred by Gurkha knives at Goose Green, often being cut up into little pieces. That this was fake news can easily be deduced from the figure that Argentine Army casualties in the entire war totalled 194.

On the Argentine side, sailor Rubén Otero was one of the 770 survivors of the ARA General Belgrano, torpedoed with the loss of 323 lives outside the exclusion zone on May 2 (the play’s take on this is less harsh than, say, the MP Tam Dalyell in Britain). Otero spent over 40 hours freezing on a raft before being finally rescued but far from hating everything British after this ordeal, his favourite pastime is drumming passionately on a band dedicated to Beatle music (the other two Argentine cast members are guitarists who perform during the play).

Gabriel Sagastume was a reluctant soldier who is now a lawyer. He bears witness to the fact that the war dead are not always the fault of the other side. Sagastume is the only survivor of a starving platoon (despite all the supplies sent from the mainland) which raided an empty cottage across the Murrell River near Stanley for food while he stayed on the other side keeping watch, only for one of them to step on a landmine on the way back, blowing all four soldiers into pieces – the landmine was, of course, Argentine. As good a reason to call the play Campo Minado as any.

Marcelo Vallejo spent the occupation manning a mortar on Wireless Ridge, around four miles west of Stanley. He had perhaps the most traumatic postwar adaptation of the trio, as he tells Jackson in the therapy session, but has since become a champion athlete and superbly fit in his mid-sixties.

Any criticisms? Just one – the background music is ample and apt but somehow manages to omit Rod Stewart’s ‘We are sailing,’ the British war anthem (at least for BFBS), especially during the 46 days between sailing out of Portsmouth and landing at San Carlos Bay. 

The play is basically a chronology of the war starting and finishing with Armour, enriched by the testimony of its participants, but no intention of being a spoiler for this masterpiece of Lola Arias. Just try and see it today or tomorrow.

(The above is this year’s last column since its author will be back in Britain all next month. ‘Beyond the headlines’ will return early next year but not for long – this column will morph into ‘Campaign comments’ by mid-February at the latest when Neuquén goes to the polls, continuing with electoral analysis pretty much throughout 2027

news.title: Zeldin touts 'best case scenario' after massive controlled detonation in Iowa
news.text: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin described initial air monitoring results following Wednesday's controlled detonation of a hazardous chemical stockpile in Iowa as a "best case scenario," as officials prepare to release the results of additional environmental testing. Speaking in an interview on Fox News Friday, Zeldin said four air monitoring stations positioned downwind of the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant recorded no detectable airborne lead following the controlled detonation. "We only have measurements of 0.0, sometimes referred to as zero detect, sometimes referred to as non detect," Zeldin said. "It's not that we just had a small elevation of lead being detected in our air monitoring," Zeldin added. "We had 0.0 readings on our air monitoring, and that's certainly a best case scenario." US ARMY TO PROCEED WITH IOWA DETONATION OF DEGRADED BOMB MATERIALS: ‘A CONSENSUS DECISION’ While the air monitoring results have been encouraging, Zeldin emphasized that the agency is continuing its environmental assessment, comparing thousands of samples collected before and after the detonation. "We are going to make sure we do all of our due diligence," he said. The EPA administrator said the agency expects to begin releasing the first post-detonation sampling results as early as Friday night. "Hopefully that confirms what we saw at the air monitor," he said. The agency's ongoing assessment comes after Wednesday's controlled detonation of the bomb-making chemical in Middletown, Iowa. DR MARC SIEGEL: IOWA'S CANCER RATE IS RISING. ONE ANSWER MAY BE FOUND IN THE WATER Roughly five tons of degraded lead azide were destroyed after being deemed unsafe and unstable, amid concerns that a plume of potentially toxic dust could drift toward Missouri in the wake of the blast. The EPA has collected more than 3,000 air, water, soil and dust samples, including 1,639 before the detonation to establish a baseline and 1,618 afterward to assess potential environmental changes. In a separate update Friday, the EPA reported that it had completed 88% of post-detonation sampling at homes where samples had also been collected before the blast and was working to complete the remaining assessments. The agency said air monitoring concluded Thursday afternoon after 30 consecutive hours of no detectable airborne lead. EPA REPORTS 'ZERO DETECTION OF AIRBORNE LEAD' DAY AFTER IOWA LEAD AZIDE DETONATION President Donald Trump also sought to reassure residents Thursday about their safety following the detonation. "They're 100% safe," he told reporters. He emphasized that the U.S. Army did a "phenomenal job" with the detonation. news.summary: EPA chief Lee Zeldin says air monitoring after Iowa Army Ammunition Plant detonation found zero detectable airborne lead, calling it a best case scenario.

news.title: Canada's parl handed 300,000-signature petition seeking removal of Trump's envoy
news.text: Canadian prime minister Mark Carney’s government has until January to respond to a petition signed by nearly 300,000 people calling for the removal of US Ambassador Pete Hoekstra. The petition was formally presented in the House of Commons this week.The petition, tabled by Green Party lawmaker Elizabeth May, calls on Ottawa to declare Hoekstra “persona non grata” and revoke his diplomatic status, accusing him of interfering in Canadian domestic affairs and undermining relations between the neighbouring countries.“He has been repeatedly abusive and insulting to Canadians,” May said while presenting the petition, according to Politico.She described Hoekstra as “the most undiplomatic diplomat” and said Canadians had made their position clear.“I think it's important to note that Canadians overwhelmingly have, on this e-petition, spoken clearly that they believe that Pete Hoekstra is not welcome in Canada,” she said.May added that more than 280,000 Canadians had “asked the government... to declare him officially persona non grata and revoke his rights to operate as a diplomat” in the country.The citizen-led petition was opened for signatures in July 2026 and remained open until November 18. It also accused Hoekstra of normalising “the Trump administration's threats to annex Canada as the 51st state”.Petitions presented in the House of Commons require the government to issue a formal response within 45 days. However, the petition is non-binding and does not compel Carney’s administration to remove the ambassador.Hoekstra, a former Republican congressman from Michigan and a staunch supporter of US president Donald Trump, took up his post in April 2025. His tenure has coincided with deteriorating relations over trade and Trump’s repeated remarks about making Canada the 51st US state.In June, Hoekstra described the prospect of annexation as “a great discussion” for Trump and Carney to have. Speaking to a Michigan radio station last year, he characterised Trump’s rhetoric as a “sign of affection” and a “generous offer”.He also described Canada’s 2025 federal election as “anti-American”, prompting Carney to respond: “That’s an interesting way of framing it.”Tensions escalated further after Hoekstra reportedly confronted an Ontario official over a provincial anti-tariff advertisement quoting former US president Ronald Reagan. Trump subsequently suspended trade negotiations.The dispute comes as both governments remain locked in a trade conflict, despite recent expressions of optimism about talks. Carney has warned that tariffs have damaged businesses and households on both sides of the border.“US tariffs have upended a trade bargain that’s existed for decades,” he said. “They’ve raised costs for American families while putting Ontario workers and businesses at a disadvantage and under a cloud of uncertainty.”The US State Department said it was aware of the petition. news.title: Netanyahu ready to offer power-sharing deal to rival – media
news.text:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is prepared to offer his main rival, former Israel Defense Forces (IDF) chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, a deal to form a unity government under which Netanyahu would serve as prime minister after Eisenkot, several Israeli media outlets reported on Friday.

Netanyahu’s Likud-led bloc lost its parliamentary majority in the October 27 election, securing 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, while the opposition bloc led by Eisenkot’s Yashar party won 48. Two Arab-led parties secured the remaining 19 seats. President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming a government on November 8.

According to public broadcaster Kan, the offer was conveyed through unofficial channels to give Netanyahu plausible deniability. Kan said Eisenkot had rejected the proposal “at this stage.”

Eisenkot has publicly accused Likud of stalling negotiations. “Unity is not a discussion about seats or who gets to go first. It is a discussion about substance and values. Yet, to date, the Likud has shown no willingness to make progress on any substantive issue,” he wrote on X. He vowed to exhaust all options in coalition talks.

Eisenkot said his party had signed coalition agreements with the secular right-wing Yisrael Beytenu and the left-wing Democrats this week and was working to reach a similar deal with Beyachad, an alliance led by former prime ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid.

Yisrael Beytenu leader Avigdor Liberman argued on Thursday that a rotation offer from Netanyahu would be “merely a ploy” to sabotage coalition talks and trigger another election.

Netanyahu has repeatedly called for a national unity government that would not rely on the support of Arab lawmakers. Likud on Friday accused Eisenkot of seeking to establish a “dangerous left-wing government” with the backing of Arab parties.

Ra’am and the Joint List, which secured a record combined number of seats for Arab-led parties, backed Eisenkot’s candidacy for prime minister. The prospect of relying on Arab lawmakers, however, has divided his prospective coalition partners.

Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, although Herzog can grant him a two-week extension.

The coalition talks come amid renewed tensions in the Middle East. Netanyahu has reportedly been pressing US President Donald Trump to resume large-scale strikes against Iran, while Israel on Thursday bombed Beirut’s southern suburbs for the first time since agreeing to a ceasefire with Lebanon in October.

Eisenkot and other opposition figures have accused Netanyahu of seeking to reignite the war with Iran to remain in power.
news.summary:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is reportedly prepared to let Gadi Eisenkot serve first as prime minister under a rotation deal

news.title: IBM ends US visa and green card sponsorship for most consulting roles
news.text: Global technology major IBM has decided to discontinue US visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of positions within its consulting division, a business unit employing more than 150,000 people worldwide. The decision comes amid growing scrutiny by the US Government of companies that depend on foreign professionals to fill skilled positions. In a statement, IBM said its participation in US high-skilled visa programmes had gradually declined over the years. The company attributed the decision to changing workforce availability, evolving skill requirements and shifting client demands.“IBM Consulting participates in US high-skilled visa programmes to address skill shortages. That participation has been declining for a number of years, and as skill availability and client needs have evolved, we have opted to discontinue visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of such roles in IBM Consulting,” the company said. Although IBM has not publicly disclosed the full scope of the changes, reports suggest that some employees affected by the decision have been given two options: relocate to an overseas office or leave the organisation by the end of the year.Posts shared by employees on anonymous professional networking platform Blind indicate that some workers have approximately three weeks to make their decision. Those who choose not to relocate have reportedly been offered severance equivalent to three months’ pay, with December 31 set as their final working day.One employee, describing the situation on Blind, claimed they had been asked to choose between moving to India with an approximately 80 per cent reduction in salary or leaving the company. The employee also expressed concerns about having to abandon a career and personal life established in the US. These accounts have not been independently verified, and IBM has not publicly confirmed the reported relocation terms or severance arrangements. IBM’s decision comes against the backdrop of increasingly restrictive US immigration policies and heightened scrutiny of employers hiring foreign professionals. In September 2026, US President Donald Trump extended for another year the $100,000 fee introduced in 2025 for employers sponsoring certain new H-1B workers from outside the country. Trump’s administration has defended the measure as a way to prioritise American workers and graduates while discouraging companies from using foreign labour when qualified domestic candidates are available. According to the White House, extending the proclamation would help safeguard US economic and national security interests, improve employment opportunities for American workers and ensure that companies recruit foreign professionals only when their skills are essential. The developments are particularly significant for Indian technology professionals, who represent the largest group of beneficiaries under the US H-1B visa programme.For years, major technology and consulting companies have relied on skilled workers from India to support their US operations. However, rising immigration costs, stricter visa policies and changing workforce strategies are creating additional challenges for professionals seeking long-term employment in the country.IBM’s latest move also highlights the wider uncertainty facing the technology sector, where employees are already dealing with restructuring, cost-cutting measures and the growing adoption of artificial intelligence. While the full impact of IBM’s decision remains unclear, the shift could signal a broader change in how multinational technology companies approach overseas talent recruitment and US-based employment.

news.title: Stocks jump to close out an erratic week that was also Wall Street's best in more than a year
news.text:
NEW YORK — Stocks jumped on Wall Street Friday and nudged the market to its strongest week in more than a year, despite several days of erratic swings.

The S&P 500 index rose 1.6%. Technology stocks once again led the market, though the gains were much broader, with 4 out of every 5 stocks rising. The benchmark index notched a gain of 5.6% for the week, its strongest since April of 2025.

It also marks a sharp turnaround from last week, when the S&P 500 index slumped and finished more than 10% below its all-time high set last month.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the Nasdaq composite also jumped Friday and closed out with strong weekly gains.

Wall Street's path higher this week was erratic. Stocks opened with a huge rally on Monday, their best since April of 2025, which is when President Donald Trump paused most of his tariffs announced on "Liberation Day" that had sent stock markets reeling.

Markets faced turbulence on Tuesday and Wednesday, resulting in a mix of more modest losses and gains for indexes. U.S. markets were closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving.

All told, the S&P 500 rose 114.71 points to 7,297.49. The Dow gained 591.99 points, or 1.2%, to 50,774.94, and the Nasdaq rose 543.70 points, or 2.3%, to 24,129.50.

Technology stocks led the gains on Friday. Microsoft rose 0.6% and Broadcom jumped 3.8%.

Anthropic, which is the first major frontier lab to go public, rose 11% to $91.88. It remains above its IPO price of $83 per share, though it has eased back from reaching a high of $115 on its first day of trading last week.

Technology companies, especially those with an artificial intelligence focus, have been the driving force behind Wall Street's gains in 2026. They can have an equal influence in pushing the broader market lower. Those dynamics were on full display this week with the AI rally on Monday and the sector's subsequent swings throughout the rest of the week.

Companies including Nvidia and Broadcom are so valuable that their stock movements can often determine whether the market rises or falls. They were the key factor in driving the market to an all-time high last month and in also pulling it mostly lower ever since. Wall Street has grown more concerned over whether the big investments in AI will produce enough profit and justify the large stock values.

Nvidia has been especially volatile. It rose 0.8%. The company has been the face of AI development and rattled the market following the sudden resignation and then surprise reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO.

Amazon jumped 4% as the holiday-shopping season kicks off. The company is also one of the most valuable on Wall Street and has been among those focusing more on AI.

Elsewhere, retailers were mixed. Target fell 0.1%, while Macy's rose 1.2%.

Households are shopping for the holidays under a cloud of stubbornly hot inflation. The latest update this week showed that the rate of inflation worsened in October. Prices on everything from gas to groceries and clothing have been rising throughout the year, mostly because of higher energy costs.

The price for Brent crude oil, the international standard, fell 0.9% to $90.84. Oil prices have swung between $72 and $114 since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in February.

Higher oil prices have directly cut into household budgets by fueling higher gasoline prices. Indirectly, higher diesel fuel prices boosted shipping costs globally. That is on top of a trade conflict between the U.S. and much of the world that has also made many goods more expensive.

The economy remains strong, but growth is largely being driven by big tech firms spending to build AI infrastructure and spending by upper-income households.

Treasury yields rose in the bond market. The yield on the 10-year Treasury rose to 4.94% from 4.85% late Wednesday.

news.title: Hundreds of thousands still without power a day after US slammed with Thanksgiving storms
news.text:
More than 260,000 people remain without power after severe weather hit both coasts of the United States during the Thanksgiving holiday.

Eastern areas were lashed on Thursday by a powerful storm which brought high winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding. Pennsylvania remained the state worst hit by power cuts early on Friday, according to monitoring site Poweroutage.us.

Conditions are now improving, though forecasters caution that it will take some time. The West Coast also was affected by its own storms.

Flight disruption persisted, too, with hundreds more delays and cancellations reported on Friday - another busy travel day.

More than 3,400 flights within, into, or out of the US were delayed and nearly670cancelled on Friday.

On Thanksgiving, more than 2,500 US flights were delayed and more than 450 were cancelled, according to Flightaware.com. One passenger told the BBC he had been stuck at New York's LaGuardia Airport for 13 hours while trying to fly to see friends in Chicago for Thanksgiving.

Beyond the travel disruption, impacts were widespread across the East Coast, and US President Donald Trump said he would consider releasing emergency funds.

Bridges closed in Maryland due to severe winds, while waves battered beaches in Delaware as water seeped onto the boardwalk. On the wettest Thanksgiving on record in Washington, tidal waters surged and soaked runways at Reagan Washington National Airport.

Parts of some states declared states of emergencyovernight between Thursday and Friday, including New York.

Nearly 2in (5cm) of rain fell on New York City's iconic Central Park, making it the wettest Thanksgiving on record at that site as well, according to preliminary data from the NWS.

Organisers of the city's annual Macy's Thanksgiving parade have also pushed back the event to Saturday - marking the event's first postponement in its 100-year history.

In neighbouring New Jersey, there were multiple reports of closed roads and bridges, and images of floodwater blanketing city streets. Coastal flood warnings persisted for parts of New Jersey through the evening on Friday.

"This is wild," an Ocean City, New Jersey-based blogger said in a video posted on social media, as he waded through water splashing above his waist.
news.summary: More than 260,000 people remain without power after severe weather hit both coasts of the United States during the Thanksgiving holiday.

news.title: Armenia approves US control of controversial transit route
news.text:
Armenia has approved a deal granting the US a controlling stake in the company tasked with developing a Trump-backed transit corridor in the South Caucasus, despite objections from Russia and Iran.

The Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) will include a road, railway and power lines running through Armenia’s southern Syunik province along the Iranian border. The 42-km rail section would link mainland Azerbaijan to its Nakhchivan exclave as part of a wider transport route connecting Baku to Türkiye.

Washington will hold 74% of the TRIPP Development Company and appoint three of its five board members, the Armenian prime minister’s office said on Thursday. Yerevan will retain the remaining stake. The company will enjoy exclusive development and operation rights for an initial 49 years, although Armenia will retain sovereignty over the territory.

US President Donald Trump said in May that the corridor would give American energy companies access to Central Asia. He cited the project when endorsing Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, whose party secured a parliamentary majority in June.

Armenian opposition lawmakers have questioned the project’s economic and security implications, arguing that Yerevan should first secure a peace treaty with Baku and reciprocal access to transport routes.

Armenia and Azerbaijan have been at odds over Nagorno-Karabakh since the late 1980s. Baku regained control of the predominantly ethnic Armenian region in 2023, prompting local residents to flee.

At White House talks in August 2025, the two countries agreed in principle on the US-backed corridor and initialed a peace treaty. Azerbaijan insists that Armenia must first remove a constitutional reference that Baku regards as a territorial claim.

Moscow warned in April that plans for the corridor had upset the regional balance. Armenia, which hosts a Russian military base, has increasingly sought closer ties with the EU.

Russia has warned that Yerevan risks losing preferential gas prices if it turns away from economic cooperation with Moscow, which supplies around 82% of Armenia’s gas.

Iran has also voiced security concerns over the project. Ali Akbar Velayati, a foreign policy adviser to Iran’s supreme leader, said earlier this month that he had warned Armenia’s ambassador that Tehran would “break their legs” if Trump and his allies crossed Iran’s “red line.”

Tehran has repeatedly warned against any attempt to sever its land border with Armenia.
news.summary:
Armenia has approved a 74% US stake in the company behind the Trump-backed corridor linking Azerbaijan to its Nakhchivan exclave

news.title: NBC won't rerun ad opposing aid to Israel, a person familiar with the matter says
news.text:
NBC will not show the 30-second commercial opposing U.S. military aid to Israel again after it aired during its "Saturday Night Live" Thanksgiving special, a person familiar with the matter said.

Jewish and pro-Israel groups objected after the spot aired. The Wall Street Journal's Joe Flint first reported the decision Friday, Fox News said.

NBC will not run again an ad perceived as anti-Israel. The spot ran during a prime-time SNL special on Wednesday night and drew an immediate backlash from Jewish and Israeli groups. The ad portrays an American girl saving $400 to buy a new bike and then cuts to an image of a— Joe Flint (@JBFlint) November 27, 2026

NBC's senior management learned of the ad only after its broadcast, the person said, adding that NBCUniversal will review its approval process to ensure appropriate levels of scrutiny. An NBC spokesperson declined to comment, and the network has not publicly confirmed its decision.

It is unclear whether other broadcasts were scheduled on NBCUniversal platforms or whether NBC found the ad breached its advertising standards.

President Donald Trump said on Nov. 3 that the U.S. would end its roughly $4 billion in annual aid to Israel in 2027 but continue weapons sales, according to Newsweek. TheWrap reported that Trump said annual aid would stop by the end of this year.

At 8:47 a.m. Eastern on Wednesday, Semafor reporter David Weigel wrote on X that a pro-Palestinian group had purchased SNL airtime to advocate ending aid to Israel. The ad's sponsor, the Institute for Middle East Understanding Policy Project, announced it on X at 9:01 a.m., saying it "informs Americans where their tax dollars are going." The post has since received more than 850,000 views.

The group said Israeli media reports valued a proposed five-year weapons package for Israel at a minimum of $19 billion and linked it to the ad. Newsweek calculated that the sum equals roughly $361 per three seconds, so the ad's figure rounds up.

NBC broadcast the ad in primetime that night. On Thursday, Anti-Defamation League CEO Jonathan Greenblatt wrote on X that it "blatantly demonizes the Jewish state and makes false claims about the use of American taxpayer dollars." Airing it "during primetime on the eve of a family holiday isn't just insensitive. It's indefensible," he wrote.

Simon Wiesenthal Center CEO Jim Berk said in a Thursday statement shared with The Hollywood Reporter that the imagery offers "a seductive but unsubstantiated narrative." "Turning children's suffering into a prop for political theater is an unacceptable manipulation," Berk said.

On Friday, the National Jewish Advocacy Center sent NBCUniversal's chairman of global advertising and partnerships, Mark Marshall, a letter seeking records and asking what evidence supported approval, TheWrap reported.

The IMEU Policy Project said in a Friday X post that the ad "passed NBC's stringent fact-checking requirements." The group argued that American taxpayers paid for every fighter jet and tens of thousands of bombs Israel has used in Gaza, all supplied by the United States. It said it was disheartened by reports that NBC would drop the ad and that changing the network's fact-checking requirements would censor accurate ads like its own.

Meral al-Babli, 9, appears in the ad, according to the group. It said her leg was amputated after an Israeli bombing of her Gaza home killed her mother and grandmother, though Newsweek said it could not independently verify those details.

On Wednesday night, millions of Americans tuning into NBC had their living rooms lit up by the face of a beautiful nine-year-old Palestinian girl named Meral al-Babli. Meral’s leg was amputated after an Israeli bombing of her house in Gaza that also killed her mother and her— IMEU Policy Project (@imeupolicy) November 27, 2026

Aid pledges and advertising rules

The Supreme Court ruled in CBS v. Democratic National Committee in 1973 that broadcasters are not required by the Communications Act or the First Amendment to accept paid editorial advertisements.

A 10-year memorandum of understanding signed in 2016 committed the United States to $38 billion in aid to Israel over fiscal 2019 through 2028.

The IMEU Policy Project paid for the ad, "Every Three Seconds." It shows an American girl who saved $400 for a bicycle, then shifts to Gaza, where a girl missing part of a leg stands amid rubble with a crutch. "Every three seconds, our government sends $400 of taxpayer money to Israel to do this," the narrator says.

Viewers are directed to the group's "No More for Israel" campaign, which asks people to contact Congress in opposition to continued military assistance and a successor aid agreement. NBCUniversal's guidelines, updated in October, say the company generally accepts issue ads with claims that are factually grounded and fall within reasonable debate.

The Israeli-American Council told Newsweek that "NBC must come clean about how this advertisement met its own standards and ensure it is not aired again." The council has asked the Federal Communications Commission to investigate whether the ad complied with applicable rules.
